title: Payroll Assistant - Education, Tutoring & Social Work
description:
About the Role

We are a fast-paced recruitment company specialising in the education, tutoring and social work sectors. Due to the high volume of workers we support, we are looking for an organised, accurate and proactive Payroll Assistant to join our busy payroll team.

This is a hands-on role supporting the processing of payroll for a large number of temporary and contract workers. You will work closely with our recruitment and operations teams, managed service vendors and local authorities to ensure hours are received, checked and processed accurately and on time.

The successful candidate will ideally have previous payroll or payroll administration experience and be confident working with large volumes of data. Experience using Merit Payroll Software and/or managed vendor systems for submitting hours to local authorities would be highly advantageous.

This is also a great opportunity for someone who wants to develop their payroll knowledge and, over time, become confident independently running payroll from start to finish.

The Role

You will support the weekly and monthly payroll process, ensuring worker information, bookings, timesheets and hours are accurately recorded and processed within the required deadlines. This will include setting up new workers and bookings, checking timesheets, processing leavers and finishers, maintaining accurate records and assisting with payroll checks and reconciliations before payroll is finalised.

You will work closely with recruitment, operations, managed service providers and local authorities to resolve missing information, discrepancies and payroll queries. You will also respond to queries from workers, consultants and clients in a professional and timely manner, investigate any issues and ensure they are resolved efficiently.

The role will involve working with a high volume of data, producing and checking payroll reports, maintaining up-to-date records and supporting the wider payroll team with general administration and other payroll-related tasks when required.

Payroll Knowledge

You should have a good understanding of payroll principles, or be keen to develop your knowledge in areas including PAYE and income tax, National Insurance, Statutory Sick Pay, Statutory Maternity Pay, holiday pay, starters and leavers, payroll deductions, timesheets and general payroll processes.

You do not need to be an expert in every area from day one, but you should be willing to learn and develop your understanding as you gain experience in the role.

Skills & Experience

Ideally, you will have previous payroll or payroll administration experience, with experience using Merit Payroll Software or a similar payroll system being advantageous. Experience working with managed service providers or submitting hours to local authorities would also be beneficial.

You will need strong Excel and data-entry skills, excellent attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with large volumes of information. You should be organised, comfortable working to tight deadlines and able to prioritise effectively in a busy environment.

Good written and verbal communication skills are essential, as is the ability to investigate and resolve problems proactively. You should be comfortable working independently while also being a strong team player.

What We're Looking For

We are looking for someone who is accurate, reliable, organised and responsive, with a genuine interest in developing their payroll knowledge.

Our payroll environment is busy and high-volume, so you will need to be comfortable working under pressure, meeting deadlines and dealing with a variety of queries throughout the day. Attention to detail is particularly important, as even small errors can have a significant impact on workers' pay.

Most importantly, we are looking for someone who wants to learn and progress. You will initially support the payroll function, but as your knowledge and confidence develop, you will take on increasing responsibility for the overall payroll process.

Development of the Role

The long-term aim is for the successful candidate to become confident in managing payroll independently from start to finish. This will include taking responsibility for setting up new workers and bookings, checking and processing hours, managing starters and finishers, carrying out payroll checks and reconciliations, producing and reviewing payroll reports, resolving payroll queries and discrepancies, and ensuring payroll is completed accurately and on time.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a strong payroll administration background who wants to develop their skills, take on greater responsibility and progress towards becoming a fully independent payroll professional.

About the Role

As a Recovery Coordinator, you will play a vital role in supporting individuals aged 18 and over who are experiencing drug and alcohol-related challenges. Working within an integrated healthcare framework, you will deliver person-centred psychosocial interventions that empower individuals to make positive, sustainable changes and work towards their recovery goals.

You will manage a caseload of service users, undertaking comprehensive assessments, developing risk management plans and creating SMART care plans tailored to each individual's needs. Using a flexible approach that combines harm reduction and abstinence-based interventions, you will provide practical advice, guidance and structured support to help individuals improve their health, wellbeing and quality of life.

Your responsibilities will include delivering structured one-to-one interventions, facilitating group-work sessions and supporting structured treatment programmes. You will use motivational interviewing techniques to engage service users, encourage positive behaviour change and promote long-term recovery.

Building effective partnerships with housing providers, employment services, healthcare professionals, probation, the criminal justice sector and other community organisations will be essential to ensuring continuity of care and addressing the wider needs of the people you support.

You will contribute to service performance targets and positive outcomes, working collaboratively with colleagues, partner agencies and local commissioners to deliver high-quality, recovery-focused services. You will also maintain accurate records, participate in clinical supervision and ensure that safeguarding, equality, diversity and inclusion are embedded in your practice.

Flexibility is important, as the role may occasionally require evening or weekend working, with reasonable notice, to meet service user needs and maintain continuity of care.

About You

You are a compassionate, motivated and recovery-focused professional with experience of working within substance misuse services and a genuine commitment to helping people achieve meaningful, lasting change. You understand that recovery is different for everyone and can adapt your approach to meet individual needs, whether through harm reduction, abstinence-based support or a combination of both.

You will bring experience of conducting comprehensive assessments, developing risk management plans and implementing SMART care plans, alongside the ability to deliver structured psychosocial interventions and facilitate both individual and group sessions. You will be confident using motivational interviewing techniques to build trusting relationships, encourage engagement and support service users to take ownership of their recovery.

You will also have:
- A sound understanding of substance misuse, addiction, the recovery agenda and the challenges faced by individuals affected by drug and alcohol use.
- A thorough knowledge of, and commitment to, the 12-step process of recovery from addiction.
- An understanding of safeguarding, risk management, equality, diversity and inclusion, and the importance of delivering safe, accessible and person-centred services.
- Knowledge of community support services, holistic care needs and the importance of effective throughcare and continuity of care.
- An understanding of the criminal justice sector and the needs of individuals accessing support in community or prison settings.
- Experience of working collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams and external partner agencies to improve outcomes for service users.
- Strong IT, communication, organisational and record-keeping skills, with the ability to manage a caseload effectively and work towards agreed targets.
- An understanding of NHS health and wellbeing outcomes and the importance of measuring progress and demonstrating positive results.
- A commitment to reflective practice, professional development and making effective use of clinical supervision.

Above all, you will be non-judgemental, resilient and empathetic, with the ability to build positive relationships with people from diverse backgrounds. You will be passionate about promoting recovery, reducing harm, tackling health inequalities and helping individuals develop the confidence, skills and support networks they need to move forward with their lives.

About Us

We are The Forward Trust, the social enterprise with charitable status that empowers people to break the often interlinked cycles of crime and addiction to move forward with their lives. For more than 25 years we have been working with people to build positive and productive lives, whatever their past. We believe that anyone is capable of lasting change. description: This role support to deliver a comprehensive reception, administrative, and clerical service that supports the multidisciplinary team in providing patient care within the department. Additionally, to offer a welcoming and professional front-of-house experience for all patients and their families receiving care at The Princess Alexandra Hospital. The role is a fixed term contract until February 2027. The Ward Clerk provides an efficient, accurate and welcoming administrative service that supports the safe and smooth running of the ward. The post holder acts as a key point of contact for patients, relatives, carers, clinical teams and partner services; maintains complete and timely patient information; and supports admissions, transfers, discharge processes and day-to-day ward organisation. In a Care of the Elderly setting, the post holder will communicate patiently and respectfully with people who may be frail, anxious, hearing or visually impaired, living with dementia or delirium, or dependent on relatives and carers for support. The Ward Clerk will recognise the limits of the role, maintain confidentiality and promptly refer clinical questions, safeguarding concerns or changes in a person's condition to a registered practitioner. The Ward Clerk is a key member of the multidisciplinary team and is responsible for providing a comprehensive, efficient and professional administrative service to support the delivery of high-quality patient care within the ward environment. Acting as a central point of communication, the post holder will work closely with nursing, medical, therapy and administrative colleagues to ensure the smooth day-to-day operation of the ward. The post holder will be responsible for managing a wide range of administrative duties, including maintaining accurate patient information, supporting admission, transfer and discharge processes, preparing and filing documentation, and ensuring patient records are available and up to date. They will be expected to use a variety of electronic patient record systems and administrative databases, ensuring all information is entered accurately and in a timely manner. As the first point of contact for many patients, relatives and visitors, the Ward Clerk will provide a welcoming and professional reception service, responding to enquiries both in person and over the telephone. The role requires excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to deal sensitively and professionally with individuals who may be anxious, distressed or have additional communication needs. The post holder will ensure that enquiries are directed appropriately and that messages are communicated promptly and accurately to the relevant members of the clinical team. Working within a busy ward environment, the Ward Clerk will support the coordination of patient flow by assisting with admissions, bed moves, transfers and discharges. This includes preparing documentation, arranging transport where required, processing referrals and appointments, and liaising with internal and external departments to ensure patient journeys are managed efficiently. The role requires strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise a varied workload while maintaining attention to detail. The post holder will provide administrative support to the wider multidisciplinary team, including preparing correspondence, photocopying, scanning and distributing documents, maintaining filing systems, ordering stationery and office supplies, and supporting ward meetings and operational activities as required. They will contribute to maintaining an organised, professional and efficient ward environment, ensuring administrative processes run smoothly and effectively. A significant aspect of the role involves working within a Care of the Elderly setting, supporting patients who may be frail, living with dementia, experiencing confusion or managing multiple long-term conditions. The post holder will be expected to demonstrate compassion, patience and understanding at all times, adapting their communication style to meet individual patient needs while maintaining dignity, privacy and respect. The Ward Clerk will be responsible for maintaining confidentiality and handling sensitive information in accordance with Trust policies, information governance standards and data protection legislation. They will ensure that all patient records, correspondence and documentation are managed securely and accurately, recognising the importance of high-quality information in supporting safe patient care. The post holder will contribute to maintaining quality and safety standards by complying with Trust policies and procedures, including infection prevention and control, health and safety, safeguarding and equality and diversity requirements. They will participate in mandatory training, team meetings, appraisal processes and service improvement initiatives, demonstrating a commitment to continuous learning and development. This role requires an individual who is organised, adaptable and able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. The successful candidate will have excellent customer service skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to remain calm and professional in a fast-paced healthcare environment. They will play an essential role in ensuring the ward functions efficiently, enabling clinical colleagues to focus on delivering outstanding patient care and contributing positively to the overall patient experience.
